changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For heads of payments: "See where you're leaving money on the table, market by market. We'll show you your own approvals by country, card type and issuer, the reason behind each decline, and the fixes we'd make." Use "approvals", not "authorization". Keep the average uplift and product names (Authorization Boost, Adaptive Acceptance) out of the opener and bring them in only as the fix for a specific market.
changes.why: Stefan rejected the average-uplift deck with "What's mine?" and "I can't take an average to my CFO", called the per-market analysis of his own approvals the most useful thing we sent, and uses "approvals" and "money left on the table" himself.

changes.change: Counter for when a competitor proposes a test on the customer's traffic (for example a local-acquiring pitch): "Before you move traffic, let us show you your approvals by country, card type and issuer, and why, from the traffic we already process." Only add a turnaround promise once the payments performance team confirms one they can meet; this deal's analysis took three weeks.
changes.why: Adyen won by offering per-country results on Kestrel's own traffic, while our equivalent analysis already existed in-house but arrived three weeks after it was requested, after the test had finished.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: "A named payments expert who reviews your approvals with you every month, market by market." Position the per-market approval review as a standing deliverable rather than something sales has to escalate for.
changes.why: Stefan asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and we had no name, and he said he only heard from Stripe when he said he was leaving.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For deals a CFO approves on a head of payments' recommendation: offer a one-page business case in the customer's own numbers, e.g. "Your money left on the table, by market, and what we'd recover", instead of pointing to the generic economic impact study.
changes.why: The CFO approved on Stefan's recommendation, and Stefan said he couldn't take an average to his CFO, so the proof had to be specific to Kestrel.
